state.request: Enhance Empirical initialization and global agent installation UX. When the empirical-init skill initializes or repairs a repository, present a polished settings wizard before persisting configuration. The wizard must expose evidence policy (required criterion evidence, real-browser checks for UI criteria, UI screenshots, and code review), Git/worktree isolation (mode, base branch, sibling path, and branch pattern), Complex decision records, and any other currently configurable safety settings that belong in setup, while keeping internal Fast/Complex routing hidden. Use safe recommended defaults, explain dependencies between toggles, allow review/edit before confirmation, preserve existing settings during repair, and retain equivalent non-interactive MCP/private-CLI inputs. Replace the current five-row empirical install picker with a searchable, scrollable, polished terminal selector modeled on the current vercel-labs/skills npx CLI experience. Expand global skill-install targets from five agents to the broad audited agent catalog supported by the npx skills ecosystem, including names, ids, native global skill roots, detection hints, and remembered/currently-managed selection. Show detected, installed, and destination-path status; preserve exact --agent, --all, --yes, --json reconciliation and marker/path safety. Keep broad skill-install compatibility separate from executable handoff/MCP capabilities so Empirical never claims it can launch or configure a runtime that only accepts skill files. First produce a reviewable specification and an accurate terminal/conversation mockup; do not implement until the user approves.

evidence.summary: First-run forced-interactive tests prove the full recommended preview is shown before persistence, and Escape cancellation leaves both configuration and workflow state absent.
Setup, core, and MCP tests cover all four evidence toggles and verify strict enabled defaults plus durable persistence.
Wizard rendering and interaction tests cover isolation, base, sibling path, branch pattern, and decision policy while excluding routing profiles and repair limits.
Tests verify criterion-evidence disablement makes test/browser/screenshot policies inactive without erasing stored values and leaves code review independently enforceable.
Section-by-section customization, validation, effective review, edit/save flow, and mutation-free cancellation are covered, including conflicting-mode rejection before writes.
Repair tests preserve omitted/current values, preview before mutation, and repair integrations only after confirmation.
TypeScript/core, bundled MCP, JSON, and private CLI surfaces accept equivalent partial setup inputs with correct first-run and repair semantics.

Selector tests cover width-safe bounded rendering, scroll counts, status/path hints, summaries, filtering, arrows, space, Enter, Escape/Ctrl-C behavior, and terminal cleanup even when rendering throws; isolated real-TTY runs also confirmed search/install and Escape cleanup.
Catalog tests validate the pinned 7cb7db64 upstream provenance, all 73 global-capable targets, project-only rejection, safe paths, and a runtime with no catalog network or npx dependency.
Tests verify remembered/detected/managed prioritization, label/id/alias/path search, and no implicit select-all fallback.

Integration tests install five skills per selected native root, deduplicate 65 shared destinations, retain shared roots until the last dependent is removed, and preserve unmanaged, symlinked, and unsafe paths.
CLI and catalog tests cover repeatable --agent/-a, --all, --yes, --json, original-id aliases, remembered selection, manifest migration, and convergent reruns.
Tests prove broad skill targets use a separate registry/type and skill-only targets do not acquire executable handoff or project-MCP claims.
Human and JSON reports identify selected agents, unique destinations, filesystem outcomes, installed skills, verified guidance, and explicitly unverified capabilities.
Documentation/help/generated-skill smoke and npm pack dry-run verify the wizard, catalog, compatibility split, defaults, private equivalents, and packaged declarations are present.
